revisions.title: Achilles the schemer, and the question that stings
revisions.body: The Achilles and Odysseus example sharpens the dispute about willing wrongdoing. Achilles says he will leave, yet the exchange presents Odysseus as the willing schemer; Hippias therefore objects that the laws punish willing wrongdoers more severely. The example turns the question of who lies into a question about whether willingness makes the act worse.
The contrast is conditional rather than absolute: the wise man can lie consistently if he wishes, while the ignorant man may happen to tell the truth.
